SR-001.justification: A descriptor to a file, left inheritable by clearing close-on-exec, does not exist in the caged child (fd_is_open false). With 1,000 inheritable descriptors open, the child counts 0 fds of 3 or more. The sweep in sys.rs (mark_fds) uses only proc_info via proc_pidinfo, fcntl and getdtablesize on a parent-allocated buffer. Skipping the sweep fails both tests.

SR-002.justification: A descriptor handed over with spawn_with_fds is open in the child, and naming stdout is a no-op. A closed descriptor number gives SpawnError::Fd from kept_fds; safe code cannot build a BorrowedFd for a closed fd, so the check is unit-tested. Recorded latency with 1,000 extra fds and a 1,048,576 soft limit is 0.63 ms overhead.

SR-003.justification: With the sweep in place, a failing rlimit step (NOFILE u64::MAX) still returns SpawnError::Apply{step Rlimit}. The sweep marks close-on-exec rather than closing, so std's error pipe keeps working.

SR-004.justification: A caged child starts a same-group sleeper and a setsid sleeper; dropping the handle kills the child and both sleepers within 1 s. After the caller reaps the leader, dropping still kills the remaining group member. A detached child keeps running. Skipping the descendant walk fails the first test, because the setsid sleeper survives.

SR-005.justification: An uncaged intermediary with GITHUB_TOKEN, SSH_AUTH_SOCK and a DYLD_ variable spawns a passthrough caged child. The child sees none of them, all three are listed in dropped_env, and an explicit GITHUB_TOKEN is visible. Unit tests cover every pattern (DYLD_, AWS_, LD_*, SSH_AUTH_SOCK, the _TOKEN, _SECRET, _PASSWORD and _API_KEY suffixes). An empty denylist fails the caged test.

SR-006.justification: Two spawns with a tmpdir grant get different TMPDIRs, each child writes its own, both directories are gone after the handles drop, and binding tmpdir explicitly is GrantError::Reserved. The directory is created with mode 0700 (DirBuilder). Not removing it on drop fails the test.

SR-007.justification: I reviewed the docs. The macos module docs list each observed hygiene behaviour, backed by named tests, and keep the double-fork escape, pseudo-terminals, the base profile and /dev/null as not done. The crate docs, README and threat-model release status say the same. Escape-class statuses are unchanged and the catalog gate passes.
